A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, retaining the title, authors, central problem, and principal theoretical results. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments on calibration, prediction accuracy, variance reduction, and sampling sensitivity in Section 6, Figures 1–7, and Table 1.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments, loss-function comparisons, model-mismatch analyses, and a learned graph from Beijing air-quality data, including results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The sampling-based MMD training framework with score-function gradients and control variates remains. v2 adds an energy-distance/CRPS training objective in Section 6.3 and a GRU followed by a GNN for the air-quality application in Appendix C.5. Equation 9 also corrects the printed MMD estimator; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change.

E1.justification: v1 uses only synthetic graph-conditioned regression data. v2 retains that coverage and adds measured Beijing air-quality time series from urban sensors in Appendix C.5, extending the work to a real-world temporal domain. This is a qualitative application rather than a quantitative calibration benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 Section 6.3 and Table 2 introduce trained loss-function comparisons absent from v1: MAE/MSE objectives associated with Franceschi/Cini, node-level objectives inspired by Kazi, an adapted Elinas ELBO, and Lpoint-MSE. Appendix C.4 specifies that these comparisons use score-function estimation. v1 mainly compared its own training variants and loss landscapes.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 changes the synthetic generator weights, kernel parameters from (0.7, 0.02) to (0.04, 0.5), Adam coefficients, initial learning rate from 0.1 to 0.05, and theta initialization from U(0.25, 0.35) to U(0, 0.1). Figure 2 changes prediction loss from MAE to MSE. New protocols include 120-node graphs, model perturbations, constrained edge probabilities, and architecture/prior searches. The 35,000-example, 80/10/10 split remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds scalability analysis and tests of perturbed predictors, generic GNNs, and incorrectly constrained graph distributions, plus the air-quality case study. The variance-reduction and fixed-versus-joint-training analyses remain. v1's loss-landscape experiment and detailed adjacency-sample-count/learning-rate sensitivity study are removed; only the latter's main takeaway survives in Section 5.4.

E5.justification: Figure 2's reported averaging changes from 20 model initializations in v1 to 8 in v2, while both retain mean plus or minus one standard deviation. v2 also reports eight independent runs for Table 1 and introduces Welch's t-test with p < 0.01 for Table 2. These are limited changes to replication and statistical reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results: Table 2 reports calibration MAE of 0.009 ± 0.001 for MMD, 0.010 ± 0.002 for CRPS, 0.025 ± 0.001 for Lpoint-MSE, and 0.082–0.087 for literature losses. It also reports model-mismatch outcomes and calibration MAE 0.003 for 120 nodes. Figure 2 and learned-parameter heatmaps are updated under changed settings, so they do not establish same-setting improvements over v1. The earlier landscape and sampling-sensitivity result entries are removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition A.2, Lemma A.3, and proofs establishing the injectivity condition for a one-layer GNN with bijective activation when the input support contains a ball. It also corrects Equation 9's missing factor of two, the control-variate formulation in Equation 11 and Appendix B, and the distinct-matrix minimum in Corollary A.1's proof. These substantively extend and repair the mathematics while retaining Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 5.2.

C1.justification: The central claims about point-prediction losses failing to guarantee calibration and distributional optimization enabling joint calibration and optimal prediction remain. Contribution 4 changes from demonstrating successful joint learning in v1 to claiming superiority over existing methods in v2. This adds a comparative claim within the retained research objective.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion: it interprets mismatch experiments as practical robustness beyond Assumption 3.1, explains self-loop identification failures and compensating spurious edges, and discusses the parameter-to-data limitation for large graphs. Appendix C.5 explicitly qualifies the physical-distance graph as uncertain ground truth. v1 primarily discussed computational overhead and deferred real-world applications to future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and substantially expands Appendix C with perturbation construction, GNN layer configurations, baseline gradients, ELBO prior/noise searches, and the temporal model description. It newly states validation-based kernel tuning. Reported training resources change from a few tens of minutes and approximately 2 GB to a few minutes and approximately 1 GB on the same hardware; the PDFs do not isolate an efficiency improvement.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands from a short GSL discussion into treatments of graph learning, output calibration, and deep latent-variable models. New positioning addresses graph signal processing and Bayesian uncertainty, including Wasserman and Mateos, and distinguishes latent-distribution calibration from output calibration and latent-space regularization. Numerous corresponding works are newly cited.

P1.justification: v2 substantially restructures the explanatory narrative: related work gains thematic subsections, the introduction expands the rationale for synthetic validation, and the experimental discussion shifts from landscape and sampling sensitivity to scalability, misspecification, and comparisons. Appendix C is reorganized around the revised experiments, while the conclusion is shortened. Much of the core problem formulation remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. v2 combines the existing graph schematic and true-parameter heatmap into main-text Figure 1 while retaining appendix versions, relocates and updates learned-parameter displays, and removes the landscape and sampling-sensitivity displays. New comparison tables, robustness heatmaps, a larger-graph visualization, and the air-quality map substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's empirical support by adding trained literature-loss comparisons and explicit tests of model misspecification, strengthening evidence for the central joint-learning claim. The new injectivity proof, corrected formulas, and expanded reproducibility information also improve the foundation of the work. Removing sampling-sensitivity evidence and reducing reported runs from 20 to 8 are material tradeoffs, and the real-world example remains qualitative. Nevertheless, the comparative and robustness evidence provides a substantial net improvement, independently of lower scores obtained under changed settings.
